title: Patch: the queue's waiting-room readout reads the last hour through indexes, not every game ever played
thread:
**Issue #1996 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1996: Patch: the queue's waiting-room readout reads the last hour through indexes, not every game ever played
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

While a player waits in the queue or hosts a room, their page asks the server every two seconds how busy play has been in the last hour. To answer, the database today reads through every finished game and every queue ticket ever written. Each poll therefore gets slower as the game's history grows, and every waiting player adds another. After this, two indexes let the database read just the last hour. Players see the same numbers, served faster; the database does a small fraction of the work.

## Why

- `GET /api/queue/population` (`crates/server/src/api/queue.rs:1452-1457`) runs two queries:
  - `tickets_recent_waits`: `... from public.tickets where status = 'claimed' and claimed_at >= $1` (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:3916-3927`);
  - `results_count_since`: `select count(*) from public.results where ended_at >= $1` (`pg.rs:6425-6436`).
- No index leads with `results.ended_at`: there are only `(p1_profile_id, ended_at)`, `(p2_profile_id, ended_at)` (`crates/server/migrations/0004_matches.sql:389-390`) and the winner index (`0056_foreign_key_indexes.sql:50`).
- None leads with `tickets.claimed_at` (`0004_matches.sql:325`, `0008_queue_modes.sql:88`, `0056_foreign_key_indexes.sql:42,58`).
- Neither table is ever purged. The retention purge's list in `crates/server/src/api/retention.rs` names neither.
- Every waiting client polls every `SERIES_POLL_SECONDS` (2 s, `crates/server/src/config.rs:816`; `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx:510-513`, `refreshPopulation` at `:862`), and the server caches nothing.
- The hourly `game_records_unfiled` scan on `matches.ended_at` (`pg.rs:4801-4818`) has the same shape.

## Proposal

- Add a migration with:
  - `results (ended_at)`;
  - a partial `tickets (claimed_at) where status = 'claimed'`;
  - a partial `matches (ended_at) where status = 'over'` for the unfiled scan.
- Optionally keep the readout's answer for a few seconds, under a named constant in the server's `config.rs`, so all waiting clients share one read.

## Where it lands

- A new migration in `crates/server/migrations/` and its line in `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs`
- A new check in `crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql`
- `crates/server/README.md`'s migration notes
- `crates/server/src/api/queue.rs` and `crates/server/src/config.rs`, only if the answer is kept

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The SQL suite: with `enable_seqscan` off, `EXPLAIN` of each readout query and of the unfiled scan shows no sequential scan of `results`, `tickets` or `matches`.
- [ ] The migration is pinned, and both Docker db suites are green.
- [ ] If the answer is kept: two readout calls inside its window reach the store once (a server test).

## Size and risks

Medium (a migration): 3 to 5 files and under 100 lines. Building an index on a large table briefly holds writes to it. These tables are small today, so a plain `create index` in the migration is fine.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40330944183)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`GET /api/queue/population` (`crates/server/src/api/queue.rs`, `population_route`) polls `tickets_recent_waits` and `results_count_since` every 2 s per waiting client, and each call seq-scans `tickets` and `results`; the hourly unfiled-records scan seq-scans `matches` the same way. Done means a new migration adds three indexes so all three queries read only the last hour, a `CHECK 20` pins them in the SQL suite, and the readout answer is kept for 5 s under one named constant so waiting clients share a single store read. Players see the same numbers.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/migrations/0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql` | new | Three `create index if not exists` statements with a 0056-style header comment |
| `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs` | change | One `MIGRATIONS` entry after the `0061` block (~line 262) |
| `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` | change | One `PINNED` line after `0061` (~line 87) |
| `crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql` | change | New `CHECK 20` before `=== ALL CHECKS RAN ===` (after CHECK 19, ~line 1102) |
| `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` | change | Migrations loop `0028-0061` gains `0062_queue_readout_indexes` |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | One paragraph after the `Migration 0061` paragraph (~line 906) |
| `crates/server/src/config.rs` | change | `QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` after `QUEUE_WAIT_STEP_SECONDS` (~line 414) |
| `crates/server/src/api/queue.rs` | change | `KeptPopulation` struct; `population_route` keeps and serves the kept answer |
| `crates/server/src/app.rs` | change | `App.queue_readout` field (~line 70) plus `build()` literal (~line 964) |
| `crates/server/tests/support/test_app.rs` | change | `App` literal gains `queue_readout` (~line 140) |
| `crates/server/tests/api/queue.rs` | change | TTL import; new kept-answer test in `mod r640002_the_queue_readout` |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`; `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`; `apps/web/` (same numbers, no client change); `spec/` (no new ruling — the kept answer is the same R640002 numbers seconds stale, which the maintainer's comment approves); `export_config.rs` and `serverConfig.ts` (the client never reads the TTL). Governing spec: §9.5 and §11 R640002 (`spec/rulings/R640002.md`).

## Steps

1. Write `crates/server/migrations/0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql`. Copy the header-comment shape of `0056_foreign_key_indexes.sql` (what each index serves, `if not exists`, plain build holds writes briefly — tables are small). Body:
   `create index if not exists results_ended_at_idx on public.results (ended_at);`
   `create index if not exists tickets_claimed_at_idx on public.tickets (claimed_at) where status = 'claimed';`
   `create index if not exists matches_over_ended_at_idx on public.matches (ended_at) where status = 'over';`
   Partial predicates match the queries' equality filters exactly (`tickets_recent_waits` filters `status = 'claimed'`, `game_records_unfiled` filters `m.status = 'over'`); `results_count_since` has no other predicate so its index is whole. Rejected: composite `(status, claimed_at)` — bigger, and 0008's `tickets_queued_mode_idx` sets the partial precedent.
2. In `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, add `("0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql", include_str!("../../migrations/0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql"))` after the `0061` tuple.
3. Run `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store migrations_are_append_only`; it fails naming the unpinned file with its checksum. Add that exact `("0062_queue_readout_indexes.sql", "<sum>"),` line to `PINNED` after `0061`, then re-run green.
4. In `crates/server/tests/sql/01_schema_invariants.sql`, add `CHECK 20` after CHECK 19's block: a `do $$` block that collects the three names from `(values (...), (...), (...))`, anti-joins `pg_class`/`pg_index` for a valid btree index, `raise exception 'FAIL (CHECK 20): ...'` on any missing, else `raise notice 'OK (CHECK 20): ...'`. Copy CHECK 19's `pg_index`/`indisvalid`/`pg_am` join shape, simplified to name lookup. Rejected: asserting on `EXPLAIN` text in-suite — planner-version-fragile; EXPLAIN is the manual gate in step 9.
5. In `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`, append `0062_queue_readout_indexes` to the `0028-0061` loop. No check-file loop change (CHECK 20 extends file `01`, no new file).
6. In `crates/server/README.md`, add one paragraph after the `Migration 0062`… after the `Migration 0061` paragraph: what each of the three indexes serves (`tickets_recent_waits`, `results_count_since`, `game_records_unfiled` in `src/db/pg.rs`) and that only indexes are added.
7. In `crates/server/src/config.rs`, after `QUEUE_WAIT_STEP_SECONDS`, add with an R640002 doc comment: `pub const QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS: i64 = 5;` — 5 s covers two `SERIES_POLL_SECONDS` cycles plus jitter with staleness negligible against the 3600 s window. Rejected: 2 s (a jittered poll re-reads every cycle) and 60 s (visibly stale while the queue moves). Do not add it to `tests/export_config.rs` — the client imports nothing new.
8. In `crates/server/src/api/queue.rs`: add `QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` to the existing `use crate::config::{...}` list and `use crate::api::stats::cached_ok;` (copy `ci_runs.rs:24`). Add after `QueuePresence`:
   `#[derive(Default)] pub struct KeptPopulation { kept: Mutex<Option<(i64, Value)>> }`
   with `fn get(&self, now: i64) -> Option<Value>` (clone the body when `now - made_at < TTL * MS_PER_SECOND as i64`) and `fn keep(&self, now: i64, body: Value)`, using the inline `lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())` pattern from `QueuePresence::touch` (`Mutex` and `Value` are already imported). Rewrite `population_route`: `let now = now_ms(); if let Some(body) = app.queue_readout.get(now) { return Ok(cached_ok(body, QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)); }`, else compute as today, `let body = json!({...})`, `app.queue_readout.keep(now, body.clone()); Ok(cached_ok(body, QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS))`. One global cell suffices — the route takes no parameters. Cite R640002 on the struct.
9. Run `grep -rn "queue_presence:" crates/server/src crates/server/tests` (today: `app.rs` struct, `app.rs` `build()`, `test_app.rs` literal). Add `pub queue_readout: api::queue::KeptPopulation,` with an R640002 doc line beside `queue_presence` in the struct, and `queue_readout: api::queue::KeptPopulation::default(),` in every `App` literal the grep shows.
10. In `crates/server/tests/api/queue.rs`, add `QUEUE_READOUT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` to the config import, and in `mod r640002_the_queue_readout` add `r640002_the_readout_is_kept_for_its_ttl` (`#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`, copy the module's `claimed_pair`/`ended` helpers): GET via `call` (which returns headers, unlike `request`) on an empty store → all-null/0 answer with `cache-control: public, max-age=5`; seed waits and games; GET again → still the empty answer (store not re-read); `tokio::time::advance(TTL*1000 + 1)`; GET → fresh numbers. This behaviorally proves two calls in the window reach the store once. The existing `r640002_reports_…` test (single GET via `request`) is unaffected.
11. Verify EXPLAIN manually: `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`, then against its leftover `jackioh-pg-test` container run each readout-shaped query with `set enable_seqscan = off` — `tickets`: `select mode, enqueued_at, claimed_at from public.tickets where status = 'claimed' and claimed_at >= to_timestamp(<ms>::double precision / 1000.0) order by claimed_at, id`; `results`: `select count(*) from public.results where ended_at >= to_timestamp(...)`; `matches`: the full `game_records_unfiled` select with two literal bounds. Assert no `Seq Scan on public.tickets/results/matches` in any plan.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r640002` — the existing readout tests plus the new TTL test.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store migrations` — pinned checksums and the embed-every-file check.
- `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo jackioh spec check` (new R640002 code cites, no note added).
- `sh crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` (Docker; green, including the manual EXPLAIN gate in step 11).

## Done when

- [ ] `EXPLAIN` with `enable_seqscan` off shows no sequential scan of `results`, `tickets`, or `matches` for the three queries.
- [ ] Migration `0062` is pinned (`migrations_pinned.rs`) and both Docker db suites pass.
- [ ] Two readout calls inside the TTL return one computed answer (new server test green) with `max-age` equal to the TTL.
- [ ] fmt, clippy, spec check green; no other file changed.

## Risks

- Index builds briefly hold writes; tables are small, so plain `create index` inside the migration's transaction is required (`concurrently` cannot run there, and `run.sh` applies with `-1`).
- The 5 s kept answer is stale by design; R640002's window semantics are unchanged and the maintainer approved approximate numbers.
- `population` gains a `Cache-Control` header; the existing test drops headers via `request()`, so it cannot break — the new test asserts the header via `call()`.
- `App` gains a field: every construction site must be updated together (step 9's grep is the guard).

## Open questions

None. The one judgment the task left (cache TTL) is decided above; no person-only step exists.
```
